analysis: The PR adds a persistent terminal test gate. EngineV2Bridge.swift head lines 506-513 declare `_testPersistentBeforeNativeTerminal` and `_testInstallPersistentTerminalGate`. EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift head line 141 awaits the gate before the native terminal. The patch places all of this inside an `#if DEBUG` region. In the patch, the declarations at lines 503-513 follow the existing `#if DEBUG` at base line 502 and precede the `#endif` at base line 527. In Events.swift, line 141 sits inside the `#if DEBUG` that opens at head line 136 and closes at line 142. Release builds therefore exclude the gate, so there is no production attack surface from it. In a DEBUG build the gate can stall the pump before `sawTerminal` is set and before the following steps: usage recording, `finishAndEmit`, `nativeRetirement.wait()`, KV release, and prefix-cache staging completion, `markReadyReceiptTerminal` and resident evidence cleanup. Those steps matter for the T-041 resource-release and cache lifecycle paths, and for T-010 and T-016-style availability. The gate is test-installed only and its comment says it is never emitted to logging or telemetry. It is not reachable from the coordinator or any consumer. It is a closure injected by tests and runs in the same process. It receives only a `CBv2Usage` value, not prompt or response text. No change to the TB-002 wire contract, attestation, authorization, encryption, billing or cache storage behavior is visible. One residual dependency is outside the supplied evidence: the DEBUG-only guarantee depends on the `#if DEBUG` guards staying intact and on release builds not defining DEBUG. I did not verify build configuration, so I treat this as an unverified contract and not a finding. I found nothing that needs a threat-model update.
